reason: The test answers a different question than the claim. In goldfish_turn.py a mulligan is `hand = deck[:7]` on a fresh shuffle: seven cards, no bottoming, up to GOLDFISH_MAX_MULLIGANS=2. There is no 'mulligan to six' in the model, so the comparison group is a free redraw of seven, which flatters the mulligan arm and will make any keep look worse than 'a random six'. The group is also selected: the sent-to-redraw games are the ones whose first seven had <2 or >5 lands, so its first seven is not a random hand even before the redraw. Only first_seven_lands is recorded, not the first seven's contents, so the 'no commander-enabler or payoff' bucket cannot be cut from existing games without re-running with new capture code. Fix: (1) compare the bucket to ALL games with a keepable seven, split by 'has a payoff/commander-enabler' vs not, which is the real question; (2) if a six is wanted, state that it needs a model change (a bottoming mulligan), which is not 'a bucket cut of existing games'; (3) print the keep-rule caveat as a limit on the claim, not just a footnote; (4) report P(commander by T4/T5) AND median first-cast turn, not one gate, and per standing rule do not headline a single row. Cheaper explanation: one 7-card keep that missed in 1 game of 4 is variance, and the pod's own log (engine ran, 'felt right', raced by a faster deck) already puts the cause on Alex's deck.
cheaper_explanation: One bad draw in one game; the log's cause is 'raced', and Sean said sequencing felt right.

Q003's 0.15-turn gap is a goldfish figure for a policy that casts each commander as soon as it is affordable, so it says nothing about the cost of HOLDING; using it as the hold cost is a category slip. The goldfish has no wheel-turn metric, so the 'turns of growth forgone' side has no number either, and the argument as written cannot price both sides. Overlaps Q003 (killed) and Q004 (expired, same break-even) heavily; this reruns Q004 under a new name. Keep it as an argument only; do not let it touch Q005's open data question.

reason: Oracle text checked in cards.json: Grand Abolisher reads 'During your turn, your opponents can't cast spells or activate abilities of artifacts, creatures, or enchantments.' The pod's paraphrase is correct on scope (own turn only; spells plus A/C/E abilities), so the 'rules' test is already settled by the card and needs no CR 702.185 or 603.7 trip to retire the Keeper's idea. What is wrong is the replacement plan. Of the four named pieces: Negate and Stubborn Denial counter NONCREATURE spells only, and warped creatures are creature spells (Denial's ferocious clause does not change that); Flawless Maneuver gives indestructible and Deflecting Swat redirects a target, neither stops a creature spell or the end-turn artifact's effect. Only the artifact, if it is a cast spell, is a legal target, and nothing says what it is (the Context itself says it needs naming in the next log). So 'the real answer is cheap instant interaction' is not supported by these cards. Fix: split into (a) retire the Abolisher-on-his-turn idea on the oracle text, done; (b) the inventory question, how many pieces can answer a creature spell or an artifact at instant speed, as a card-search, gated on Sean naming the artifact; drop the claim that the four listed cards answer the warp turn. Also unsettled: whether Abolisher would be useful on Sean's turn is a separate point (protecting the wheel from a response), not shown here.

claim: Of the cards in the 99, only a small set can answer a creature spell or the end-the-turn artifact at instant speed (Swords to Plowshares, Get Lost, Chaos Warp, Otawara and the Commands answer permanents after they resolve; Negate and Stubborn Denial cannot touch creature spells; Deflecting Swat and Flawless Maneuver protect Sean's pieces and do not stop a warp turn), so the deck has no clean answer to the warp turn itself and the honest plan against Alex is racing it.
expected_effect: A count of the deck's answers split into stops a creature spell, answers a resolved creature or artifact, and protects only. If the first group is empty, the hypothesis is that the warp matchup is decided by speed and not by held answers.
